instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a rice cooker or a covered pot.
Meanwhile, drain the tofu. Lay the block on its widest side and cut it across into 4 flat slabs about 5/8 inch (1.5 cm) thick.
Pat the slabs dry on all sides with paper towels. Sprinkle them with the 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
In a small jug, stir together the 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake and 2 tbsp water. Keep it by the stove.
Peel the 2 garlic cloves and slice them as thin as you can. Thinly slice 1 of the green onions.
Set out three shallow bowls. Put the 2 tbsp flour in the first. Crack the egg into the second and whisk it with a fork. Mix the 4 tbsp white sesame seeds and 4 tbsp black sesame seeds in the third.

Dust a slab in the flour and shake off the extra. Dip it in the egg and let the drips fall off, then press it into the sesame seeds on both sides and the edges until it's covered. Do the same with the other 3 slabs.

Heat the 2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Add the garlic and stir it for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's golden and crisp. Watch it closely. It turns from golden to burnt fast. Lift it out onto a paper towel and leave the oil in the pan.
Turn the heat up to medium-high. Lay in the tofu slabs and cook them for about 1 1/2 minutes, until the sesame smells nutty and the underside is crisp and golden.
Turn them gently with a spatula and cook the other side for about 1 1/2 minutes, until it's crisp too.
Hold each slab on its edge with tongs and sear the edges for about 30 seconds each, until they're crisp. Transfer the tofu to a plate lined with paper towels.
Turn the heat down to medium and pour the sauce into the pan. Let it bubble for about 1 minute, until it's thick and syrupy, then take the pan off the heat.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Put a slab of tofu on each plate, spoon the sauce over it and scatter the crisp garlic and green onion on top. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: All four versions pan-fry slabs of firm tofu until golden and finish them with a soy sauce based sauce. RecipeTin Eats, the lead, coats the tofu in flour, egg and white and black sesame seeds, fries it for only about 1 1/2 minutes a side plus the edges, and spoons over a quick teriyaki of equal parts soy sauce, mirin, sake and water with crisp garlic on top. Contemplating Sweets and Kokoro Cares use starch or plain tofu with a soy and butter glaze, and Norecipes salts and weights its tofu and glazes it in a ketchup and soy sauce, so the sesame crust and the butterless sauce are the lead's own. This one follows the lead's amounts for 4 (four 3 1/2 oz slabs, so one 14 oz block), keeps its optional garlic chips, and adds the plain rice the lead suggests serving it with; the egg in the crust means it's vegetarian, not vegan.
